evidence: applier.py:671-672: `for mutation in mutations: _record_unrouted(mutation, ctx, mutations_with_outcomes)` — every leftover dict is recorded failed, not dispatched
route_for still returns LEGACY_ROUTE for actions outside NON_CREATE_FAMILIES (batch_dispatch.py:206) and an override can set a non-create family to legacy (batch_dispatch.py:214-216)
reroute_migrated_plans only migrates plans whose EVERY mutation is NON_CREATE_FAMILIES AND route_for == COORDINATOR_ROUTE (batch_dispatch.py:708-716) — a legacy-routed mutation is excluded

The retired legacy loop dispatched them. The PR characterizes the unrouted remainder as only 'a plan mixing a create with a non-create action', understating the scope.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make apply_phase.apply_mutations forward `ticket_plans` unconditionally (or raise an explicit, actionable error) so the producer matches applier._typed_batch's new hard requirement that ticket_plans not be None.
evidence: src/rebar/reconciler/apply_phase.py:121-126: `_ticket_plans_kw = ({"ticket_plans": getattr(ctx, "ticket_plans", None)} if getattr(ctx, "ticket_plans", None) is not None and _accepts_ticket_plans(applier.apply) else {})`
src/rebar/reconciler/applier.py:259-260: `if ticket_plans is None: raise TypeError("apply() batch form requires ticket_plans (ticket_planner.plan_pass)")`

src/rebar/reconciler/run_differs.py:278-279: `ctx.observation / ctx.ticket_plans are not declared on _PassContext; the plain dataclass accepts the attribute assignment` — so getattr falls back to None when run_differs did not run
src/rebar/reconciler/reconcile.py:94-95: _PassContext declares `mutations` but has no `ticket_plans` field, confirming the attribute is absent unless run_differs assigns it
Old signature had `ticket_plans=None` default (applier.py:369 still shows the keyword default for the public apply) so omitting the kwarg used to be harmless; the new _typed_batch makes None fatal
advisory.finding: apply_phase.apply_mutations forwards `ticket_plans` to applier.apply only when `ctx.ticket_plans is not None`, but applier._typed_batch now raises `TypeError("apply() batch form requires ticket_plans")` whenever ticket_plans is None. Because `ticket_plans` is not a declared `_PassContext` field (it is assigned dynamically by run_differs), any pass that reaches apply_mutations without run_differs having populated it will drop the kwarg and abort a previously-legal non-empty outbound persisting batch with TypeError, instead of the old fall-back to the legacy per-mutation loop.
scenarios: A reconcile pass whose ctx.ticket_plans was not populated by run_differs (partial ctx, early return, or a direct apply_mutations call) with a non-empty outbound batch and persist=True
Any future/alternate caller that builds a _PassContext and invokes apply_mutations without threading ticket_plans
advisory.suggested_fix: Either declare `ticket_plans` on _PassContext with a non-None default and forward it unconditionally, or change the apply_phase guard so a persisting outbound batch always forwards ticket_plans (failing loudly at the producer if run_differs did not populate it) rather than silently dropping the kwarg into a TypeError.

evidence: src/rebar/reconciler/apply_phase.py:121-126: `_ticket_plans_kw = ({"ticket_plans": getattr(ctx, "ticket_plans", None)} if getattr(ctx, "ticket_plans", None) is not None and _accepts_ticket_plans(applier.apply) else {})`

src/rebar/reconciler/applier.py:393 calls `_typed_batch(mutations, ticket_plans)` which at applier.py (_typed_batch) raises `TypeError("apply() batch form requires ticket_plans ...")` when ticket_plans is None

Mitigating: src/rebar/reconciler/run_differs.py:299 unconditionally sets `ctx.observation, ctx.ticket_plans = ticket_planner.plan_pass(...)`, and ticket_planner.plan_pass (ticket_planner.py:247, returns `tuple[Any, tuple[...]]`) always returns a tuple (empty `()` for no mutations), which is `not None` and passes the None-guard — so no concrete production ctx with None ticket_plans and outbound mutations could be cited.

ABSENCE: could not locate a reconcile/apply path that reaches apply_phase.apply_mutations with outbound mutations but ctx.ticket_plans unset/None; the break is latent, not demonstrated at a live callsite.
advisory.finding: apply_phase.apply_mutations forwards `ticket_plans` to `applier.apply` only when `ctx.ticket_plans is not None`, treating it as optional, but `applier.apply`'s batch form now raises TypeError when `ticket_plans` is None — an optional-vs-required contract asymmetry between the production caller and callee.

evidence: src/rebar/reconciler/apply_phase.py:121: `_ticket_plans_kw = ({"ticket_plans": getattr(ctx, "ticket_plans", None)} if getattr(ctx, "ticket_plans", None) is not None and _accepts_ticket_plans(applier.apply) else {})`
src/rebar/reconciler/applier.py:393: `mutations = _typed_batch(mutations, ticket_plans)` called before any partitioning
src/rebar/reconciler/applier.py:256-258: `_typed_batch` raises `TypeError("apply() batch form requires ticket_plans ...")` when `ticket_plans is None`

`getattr(ctx, "ticket_plans", None)` returns None when run_differs did not populate the attribute (run_differs.py:299 sets ctx.ticket_plans, but a ctx missing it yields None) → kwarg omitted → apply() uses its default `ticket_plans=None` → TypeError aborts the pass
advisory.finding: apply_phase.py forwards `ticket_plans` only when `ctx.ticket_plans is not None`, but `applier.apply`/`_typed_batch` now hard-require it and raise `TypeError` when absent — so a pass whose `ctx.ticket_plans` is None or unset (e.g. ctx without the attribute) will abort with TypeError instead of applying.
advisory.suggested_fix: Either always forward ticket_plans (defaulting to [] when ctx.ticket_plans is None) in apply_phase, or make apply()/_apply_batch treat an absent ticket_plans as an empty plan list rather than a TypeError when there are no outbound mutations to route.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Run _audit_rebar_id_label_writes (outbound_<action>) before _dispatch_with_backstop in reroute_ordered_create_plans so the create path keeps the G6 guard that _apply_one and make_guarded_execute both enforce.
evidence: batch_dispatch.py:516-517: `before_dispatch()` then `result = _dispatch_with_backstop(batch, ctx)` with no `_audit_rebar_id_label_writes` call
deleted applier._apply_one ran `_audit_rebar_id_label_writes(f"outbound_{action}", [_BatchAuditView(mutation)])` before dispatch (diff removes this)

make_guarded_execute.dispatch_fn preserves the guard: batch_dispatch.py:620-623 `audit._audit_rebar_id_label_writes(f"outbound_{batch.get('action','')}", [audit._BatchAuditView(batch)])` with comment 'preserve the pre-dispatch rebar-id label-write authorization guard (G6)... without it the coordinator route would bypass the guard'
_AUTHORIZED_REBAR_ID_LABEL_ACTIONS maps `outbound_create: frozenset({'create'})` (rebar_id_audit.py:90-94) — the guard is per-action and governs creates
apply_handlers.handle_create (apply_handlers.py:206-252) and _dispatch_with_backstop (batch_dispatch.py:586-599) contain no audit call — the guard was strictly caller-responsibility
blocking.finding: The create reroute (reroute_ordered_create_plans) dispatches creates via _dispatch_with_backstop WITHOUT running the rebar-id label-write authorization guard (_audit_rebar_id_label_writes). The retired _apply_one ran this guard before every dispatch, and the sibling coordinator route (make_guarded_execute.dispatch_fn) still runs it explicitly — but the create path, which is precisely the per-action-governed outbound_create leaf, now bypasses the fail-closed guard (G6).
blocking.suggested_fix: In reroute_ordered_create_plans, before line 517 _dispatch_with_backstop(batch, ctx), load rebar_id_audit and call _audit_rebar_id_label_writes(f"outbound_{batch.get('action','')}", [_BatchAuditView(batch)]) — mirroring make_guarded_execute.dispatch_fn.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Run _audit_rebar_id_label_writes on the create reroute dispatch path (reroute_ordered_create_plans/_dispatch_with_backstop) so it is enforced for every dispatched mutation, matching the coordinator route and the retired _apply_one.
evidence: Deleted _apply_one ran the guard for every dispatched mutation: applier.py (old) `_audit_rebar_id_label_writes(f"outbound_{action}", [_BatchAuditView(mutation)])` with comment 'Without this call, _audit_rebar_id_label_writes was bypassed for every legacy dict-shaped mutation'.

Create reroute dispatch at batch_dispatch.py:516-517 runs only `before_dispatch()` then `_dispatch_with_backstop(batch, ctx)`; `_dispatch_checkpoint` (applier.py:709-719) runs only abort_check + _recheck_drift, NOT the audit guard.

The parallel coordinator route DOES re-add the guard: batch_dispatch.py:620-623 `audit._audit_rebar_id_label_writes(f"outbound_{batch.get('action','')}", [audit._BatchAuditView(batch)])` with comment 'preserve the pre-dispatch rebar-id label-write authorization guard (G6) ... without it the coordinator route would bypass the guard.'

`_dispatch_with_backstop` (batch_dispatch.py:586-599) calls `apply_handlers.dispatch_mutation` directly; search_files for 'audit' in apply_handlers.py returned '(no matches)', so the guard is not re-run inside the handlers.

Guard enforcement is per-action: rebar_id_audit.py:90-94 authorizes outbound_create for {create} ONLY, and the docstring (rebar_id_audit.py:170-176) states an authorized leaf emitting an action outside its permitted set still raises.
blocking.finding: The create reroute dispatch path (reroute_ordered_create_plans -> _dispatch_with_backstop) drops the pre-dispatch rebar-id label-write authorization guard (_audit_rebar_id_label_writes) that the deleted _apply_one ran before every batch dispatch, and that the sibling coordinator reroute explicitly re-adds. An outbound create mutation can reach the vendor write without the rebar-id label-write authorization check.
scenarios: An outbound create batch dict carries an embedded rebar-id-* label op whose action is delete/update (misshapen/malicious plan); on the create reroute it is dispatched to Jira with no RebarIdLabelWriteError, whereas the legacy _apply_one and the coordinator route would have blocked it.
blocking.suggested_fix: Add the audit call inside _dispatch_with_backstop (so both the create reroute and coordinator route share it) e.g. `audit._audit_rebar_id_label_writes(f"outbound_{batch.get('action','')}", [audit._BatchAuditView(batch)])` before `apply_handlers.dispatch_mutation(batch, ctx)`, and drop the now-redundant call in make_coordinator_dispatch.
